subject: barnstormerBiplane
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: barnstormer biplane.
Style: whimsical.
reasoning:
I'm planning a module for a whimsical barnstormer biplane, aiming for a moderate 350-500 line build using the confirmed SDK helpers like part, sweep, rod, extrude, lathe, stick, cards, decal, svg, and paint to keep things stable and error-free.

For the design itself, I'm sketching a static model with no joints needed: a rounded fuselage painted red with a cream band, a big round propeller spinner, bold striped wings, struts, a tail fin and rudder, and a cartoonish cowl for charm. The plane stands on its wheels with the tail skid touching y=0, with rough dimensions around a 7.5m wingspan and 6m length, fuselage swept along the z-axis from tail to nose with a tapering radius.

Now I'm defining the fuselage as a swept shape along a curved path from tail to nose with varying cross-section radius, adding a cockpit ring and a separate ellipsoid nose cowl part, then building the wings as extruded rounded rectangular outlines with thin thickness running along the span.

Adding rounded corners with smoothing...

For wings, I'm thinking stripes with cream and red colors running spanwise for a whimsical look, and I'll add rod struts connecting the wing points at set x and y positions.

Adding cabane struts and tail geometry...

Adding gear struts and wheels...

Now for the propeller: hub at the nose with blade geometry extruded as thin slabs spanning vertically, forming a simple two-blade spinner.

Building the spinner lathe profile...

For the cockpit, I'll simplify to a dark recessed cylinder sunk into the fuselage top near y=1.58 to suggest the canopy opening, then add a small sphere for the pilot's head poking out.

For the pilot I'm going whimsical: a skin-toned head sphere at [0,1.7,0.2], small dark goggle spheres for lenses, and a flowing red scarf swept along a curved path trailing behind for motion. I'll also add a tiny flag on the tail fin and consider fuselage stripe bands for extra charm.

Now I'm working out the paint stripes around the fuselage's z-axis to create cream rings on the red body, then figuring out how to place roundel decals on the fuselage sides by finding a surface hit point near the target coordinates to anchor the decal properly.

Writing roundel SVG...

I'm naming the plane "Whimsical" and deciding to skip extra details like wing roundels and painted text for now, keeping things simple.

Now I'm settling on a color palette—red, cream, blue, yellow struts, dark accents, skin tone, goggle blue, scarf orange—and planning the geometry for the wings and cabane struts, positioning the upper and lower wings relative to the fuselage.

Working out strut positions: since the fuselage radius is only 0.4, the interplane struts need to sit at x=±1.5 and ±3.2 where the wings actually extend, connecting the lower wing around y=1.25 to the upper wing near y=2.25 at z=±0.35, with cabane struts running from the fuselage top up to the center of the upper wing.

I'm now defining the fuselage spine as a smooth curve from tail to nose, then shaping a radius function that tapers thin at the tail, widens through the mid-body, and narrows again near the nose cowl.

Checking the radius function at tail and nose, it gives similar thin values at both ends with a fatter middle, but since the nose gets its own cowl sphere added separately, round default end caps should work fine. Now I'm moving to the fuselage paint, planning to apply red and cream stripe bands along the z-axis across the sweep.

Working through the tail assembly next: positioning the fin base above the fuselage tail top, and placing the horizontal stabilizer with its chord length at the right z position. Then for the landing gear, I'm placing the main wheels so their radius brings them to touch the ground at y=0, working out the leg rods connecting the fuselage mounts down to the wheel centers, plus a small hub cylinder to cover the axle—skipping wheel fairings for simplicity. Now I'm calculating the wing's bottom surface position relative to its mounting height.

Moving to the nose, I'm sizing the engine cowl sphere and figuring out where the spinner and propeller blades sit in front of it, confirming the blades stay above ground clearance. I'm defining the spinner shape as a lathe profile swept around the fuselage axis, then working out a path for the pilot's scarf trailing back from the neck around the cockpit, using a curved spline through several points to give it a flowing look behind the open-cockpit pilot figure.

Now I'm placing small goggle spheres on either side of the pilot's head and sizing the head sphere itself, adding little whimsical touches like a nose bump, before moving on to shape the helmet.

For the helmet, I'm building it as a partial sphere capped at the top to mimic a leather aviator cap, positioning it slightly above and around the head so it reads as covering the skull properly. Next I'll add a small triangular pennant extruded off the tail fin for a bit of playful detail.

I'm thinking a trailing banner would add charm instead of just a flat pennant — sweeping a thin blue ribbon back from the tail fin using a wavy Catmull-Rom curve so it looks like it's fluttering behind the plane. Then I'll move on to painting color stripes onto the wing surfaces.

I'm setting wing stripes to run spanwise with cream and red bands, keep the lower wing solid cream, and color the tail blue. For structure I'm adding yellow strut rods between wing points and a couple of thin flying wires connecting upper and lower wingtips for realism. The fin itself I'm building as an extruded outline shape with slight corner smoothing for a rounded look, and now I'm figuring out the stripe pattern for the rudder.

Next I'm working out the fin's paint color (blue) and height, then extruding the tail stabilizer as a flat rectangular shape with smoothed corners, positioned behind the fuselage. For the main wings I'm defining upper and lower rectangular wing outlines with matching thickness and smoothing, checking that the lower wing's position intersects naturally with the fuselage. I'm considering whether to add aileron details or wing roundel decals but leaning toward skipping those for now, and starting to set up a decal/texture system for markings like the roundel.

For the decal placement, I'm computing a surface hit point on the fuselage using an azimuth/elevation lookup around a center point, with a direction vector pointing outward from the flank, then mirroring that for the opposite side of the fuselage. I'm also sketching out the builder setup, including which imports are actually needed (geometry primitives, paint/stripe helpers, SVG support) versus extras I can leave out, and noting that spheres and cylinders will handle the pilot and wheels respectively.

Now I'm finalizing the metadata and writing out the full implementation, aiming to keep it around 200 lines.
